items.caption:
Higgsfield founder Alex Mashrabov says the average prompt behind their open-source AI movie is over 3,000 words long.

He adds that each scene also uses at least 10 image references, to pin down how characters look, the background and where everyone stands. His point: real AI filmmaking workflows are far more complex than what today's benchmarks measure.

Full conversation: 20VC with Harry Stebbings and Alex Mashrabov, founder of Higgsfield.

items.caption:
Swipe to see the startup using AI to design entire buildings, not just pictures of them.

Dream builds what it calls built world models: AI that generates full building plans, including structure, plumbing and HVAC, and checks them against physics and building codes. Architects, engineers and developers use it to sketch out designs and estimate costs.

The company just came out of stealth with a $17M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz, with SV Angel, XYZ and Zigg Capital also investing. a16z partner Kimberly Tan says the firm first backed Dream more than a year ago, when it was just an idea.

Founders Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur were Stanford roommates who then spent a decade at Palantir. Their model was trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data from US permit archives, and it is already running on 10 active projects in Texas and California. The goal: replace tools like AutoCAD and Revit.

Sources: TechCrunch, Dream.

items.caption:
Swipe to see the tiny YC startup that just got bought for making products easier for AI assistants to find.

Anglera takes the messy product data stores get from suppliers, like spreadsheets, spec-sheet PDFs and images, and uses AI to fill in and fix it. When a shopper asks an AI assistant whether a part will fit, clean data is what lets the store's product show up.

Montreal-based Coveo, whose search and AI tools are used by retailers, manufacturers and tech companies, has acquired the San Francisco startup for an undisclosed amount. It is Coveo's first acquisition in five years. Its CEO said Coveo had considered building something similar, but bought Anglera because its product was already showing results and is ready to sell today.

Former Uber product managers Ray Iyer and Amay Aggarwal started Anglera in 2024 and went through Y Combinator. All five employees are joining Coveo's 800-person team, and existing Anglera customers stay on its platform.

Sources: The Globe and Mail, Dealroom, Unite.AI.

items.caption:
Swipe to see the startup that doesn't sell robots. It runs the whole factory.

Foundry Robotics builds complex electromechanical hardware, like drones, satellites, wire harnesses and underwater vehicles, for defense and commercial customers. It owns and runs the factory itself, using AI-powered robotic cells and technicians, and charges companies to manufacture for them.

The company raised an oversubscribed $100M Series A led by Marlinspike Partners. Khosla Ventures and Red Glass Ventures came back, and SE Ventures, Wing VC and Axiom Ventures joined.

The money goes into a new 130,000-square-foot factory in Emeryville, which grows its manufacturing footprint twentyfold. Founder and CEO Adarsh Kulkarni was employee number four at Ghost Robotics and later led robotics at Scale AI, and co-founder Emmanuel Lamacchia ran the Tesla Model Y program. Foundry says it can move a product from design to production in weeks.

Sources: San Francisco Business Times, Ventureburn.
